title: 一周 10 万星，AI「逆向一切」，但大家不要过于兴奋
summary: 头图图片来源：REA 头图来源：CyberSecurityNews 「在应用里看到一个想加入自己产品的功能？让智能体去帮你调查它。」 这是 REA 项目主页第一屏的话。后半句更直接：即使没有源代码，智能体也可以检查应用、解释功能怎么工作、展示证据，「并为你的项目实现类似功能」。 REA 全名 Reverse Engineer Anything，即「逆向一切」。 上周它在 AI 开发者圈刷了屏：10 月 6 日还不到 1 万星，到 10 月 12 日已经超过 11 万 。 6 天涨了 10 万星，平均每天约 1.7 万｜图片来源：Star History 真正让普通人看到这件事的，是游戏。10 月初，一批老游戏突然能在浏览器里直接玩了：《光环：战斗进化》《半条命》《暗黑破坏神》，还有真正意义上的 3A 大作《GTA5》和《使命召唤：现代战争 2》。 其中最出圈的一份复盘，来自逆向开发者 Maurice Heumann：他让十几个 Claude Code 和 Codex 智能体并行干活，把一款射击游戏 99% 的函数还原成了 C++ 源码，其中 83% 编译出来和原程序逐字节一致。他用的是 Hex-Rays 的官方 MCP，不是 REA。 也就是说，REA 只是这波浪潮里名字最响的那一个。 同一个星期，整个 AI 逆向圈都在加速。 似乎，人人都有免费软件用、免费游戏玩的日子到来了。 旧工具，新用户 逆向工程，就是手里没有源代码，从编译好的程序往回推，搞清楚它是怎么写的。这原本是安全研究员和破解者的手艺：在反编译器、反汇编器、调试器之间来回切，一个功能拆上几天是常事。 REA 干的事，是把这套工具接到 AI 编程智能体上。接口用的是 MCP，一种让 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 这类智能体调用外部工具的通用协议。 装好之后，你对智能体说一句「弄清这个应用的搜索功能怎么工作」，它会自己去调 Ghidra、IDA 或 Hopper 等对应的工具，帮你翻二进制，调 JADX 拆安卓安装包，或者直接读 Electron 应用里打包的 JavaScript，最后把结论和证据一起交回来。 智能体负责提问，REA 负责取证｜图片来源：REA 听上去像个新物种。但放在专业圈里看，它其实更像一次重新包装：毕竟让 AI 接上逆向工具，GhidraMCP、IDA Pro MCP 这些开源项目去年就在做了。 REA 走红前不久，IDA Pro MCP 的作者、调试器 x64dbg 的开发者 Duncan Ogilvie 在 X 上说，他用 IDA 的 MCP 插件，大约一小时解完了今年 Flare-On 的全部题目。 Flare-On 是谷歌旗下 FLARE 团队每年办的逆向挑战赛，题目大多取材自真实的恶意软件分析。 这并非个例，逆向领域的专家们其实普遍对今天这波新兴起的浪潮不是很看得上眼：Elias Bachaalany 是逆向工程教材《Practical Reverse Engineering》的合著者，早年在 IDA 的开发商 Hex-Rays 工作过。 REA 被各路人马转发刷屏时，他也转了其中一条推介，开头就一个词：炒作。接着他列了几个早就存在的同类工具，意思是这些人只是没见过。 逆向教材合著者的评价，开头就一个词｜图片来源：X AI 能拆程序是真的，只是不从 REA 开始。能拆到什么程度，圈内说法也不一致。 安全领域博主轩辕之风认为，没加壳的程序 AI 轻松拿下，轻度加壳也行，VMP 这类高强度虚拟化保护目前还啃不动；他还批评 REA 连动态调试都没有。一家做逆向产品的公司也在 X 上说，碰到加壳样本，模型分析照样会卡住。反方的说法是：混淆能拖慢 AI，挡不住它。 公开的案例，多数落在容易的那一头。宝玉用 Codex 加 REA 逆向了一个混淆过的网页前端，说几乎完整还原了里面的编辑器。也有博主拿它拆剪映，发现 Claude 拆到一半会卡住，也会被限制。 还有一类东西，它怎么都拿不到：放在服务器上的逻辑。你能拆开装在自己电脑上的客户端，显然拆不开别人机房里的那一半。 另外，工具多也未必是好事。Duncan Ogilvie 说过，他不认为给模型暴露更多工具能让它表现更好；现在也确实已经有 REA 用户抱怨，它塞给智能体的工具说明太长，用不了多久就把上下文挤满了。 REA 真正新的地方，其实在还是在被大幅降低的逆向门槛 。 以前想让 AI 帮你逆向，你得先是个会逆向的人：装好 IDA，配好插件，知道该问什么。现在一行 npx rea-agents setup，选好要接入的智能体、点头确认，配置就写好了。把它推上热榜的，也不是安全圈，是 AI 博主和科技大号。 REA 的技术不新，新的是用它的人。 「逆向」AI 做，「牢」用户坐 新用户带来的第一个问题，就藏在那句宣传语里：给你的项目里加上类似功能。拆开来看，和照着做一个，在法律上是两件事。 拆一个软件，法律上大致要过三个层面： 商业秘密、版权，还有合同 。 首先是商业机密，最高人民法院 2020 年关于商业秘密案件的司法解释写得很明白：对从公开渠道取得的产品做拆卸、测绘、分析，拿到技术信息，不算侵犯商业秘密。前提是东西来路正，先用不正当手段拿到秘密、再拿逆向当说辞，法院不认。 版权这部分，《计算机软件保护条例》第十七条允许为了学习和研究软件里的设计思想和原理去使用软件，2020 年修正的《著作权法》第五十条，把「计算机软件反向工程研究」列为可以避开技术措施的情形之一。 但大多数商业软件的用户协议里，都有一条禁止反编译的条款。在美国这一条是经常被引用且能执行的：2003 年的 Bowers 诉 Baystate 案里，联邦巡回上诉法院认定，软件许可里的禁止逆向条款有效，逆向之后做出竞品的一方，按违约赔了钱。 欧盟反过来，合同里禁止为互操作而反编译的条款，一律无效。同一件事，换个地方答案就不同。 《著作权法》第五十条：豁免的是「研究」｜图片来源：中国政府网 至于照着做一个，这里其实有个好消息：版权保护的是代码怎么写，不保护功能本身。条例第六条写得清楚，保护不延及开发软件所用的思想、处理过程和操作方法。单从版权看，别人有个好用的搜索功能，你自己写一个效果相似的，本身不违法。 麻烦其实出在它是怎么写出来的。软件行业应对这件事有一套老办法，叫 净室开发：一组人去拆对方的产品，只写出功能说明书；另一组从没看过对方代码的人，照着说明书从头写。 两组之间隔着一道墙，墙就是日后打官司时的证据，证明新代码是独立写出来的。 REA 现在把这道墙拆了：读反编译结果的是这个智能体，写新代码的还是这个智能体，中间没有任何隔断。Hacker News 上有人把这种做法叫作「洗知识产权」；一个复刻 Photoshop 的项目，开发者说他们团队明确禁止成员用 Ghidra 和 REA，原因很简单，怕被起诉。 游戏圈把这件事推到了极端。Maurice 那种做法叫字节级匹配反编译：写出来的源码，编译之后要和原程序一个字节都不差，他说这给了智能体一个非对即错的客观信号。净室追求的是「我没照着你写」，字节级匹配追求的恰恰是「写得和你一模一样」。 发行商的反应也很直接。 10

title: 尊界：11 月起陆续升级踏板；iPhone 折叠屏国内预约超 200 万；6 个月，超千万 Claude 账户被封杀｜极客早知道
summary: 陶哲轩提出「数学 2.0」：AI 解题之外，还要帮助人理解证明 10 月 11 日，数学家陶哲轩公开了在加州理工学院的演讲《数学 2.0》。他认为，AI 正在降低部分数学问题的求解成本，使数学研究逐渐从「证明稀缺」走向「证明富足」。但目前多数前沿问题仍未解决，不能只凭公开传播的成功案例判断 AI 的整体能力。 陶哲轩指出，得到正确证明，并不意味着研究者理解了证明为何成立，或掌握了可用于其他问题的新方法。他主张用 AI 寻找更易理解的证明、整理分散的研究成果，并对大量数学问题开展系统分析。例如，等式理论项目通过人类与自动化工具协作，对超过 2200 万个命题作出了判定。 对于 AI 解题能力的评估，他还呼吁公开计算资源消耗、失败尝试等信息。在陶哲轩看来，未来数学研究既要利用 AI 扩展探索范围，也要保留人类对证明及其现实应用的理解和判断。（来源：机器之心） Claude 爆发大规模封号潮：半年封杀 1140 万个账号申诉后仅 4.2 万翻案 10 月 11 日，据媒体报道，近期 Claude 账号封禁问题引发开发者讨论。受到关注的一项数据来自 Anthropic 今年 7 月发布的报告：2026 年上半年，平台累计封禁约 1140 万个账号；收到约 39.8 万次申诉，其中约 4.2 万次申诉成功。报告未披露完整的封禁原因分布，仅凭这些数字也无法判断近期封号是否增加，但申诉结果使平台的封禁标准和复核机制受到关注。 Anthropic 列出的违规情形包括利用服务从事违法活动、侵犯隐私，以及违反地区使用限制等。今年上半年，Anthropic 还向相关儿童安全组织提交了超过 1.5 万起报告。 此外，Anthropic 近期修订了 Claude 使用政策，计划自 11 月 12 日起禁止用户在没有明显目的的情况下，反复对模型实施极端残忍行为。公司称，新规针对的是极端情形；用户表达不满、反驳模型、创作黑暗题材内容，以及开展模型测试与研究，不属于该项禁令的范围。（来源：快科技） 英伟达洽谈收购 Reflection AI，已投资 8 亿美元，后者估值达 250 亿美元 10 月 11 日，据媒体报道，英伟达正与美国人工智能初创企业 Reflection AI 就潜在收购或进一步扩大投资展开初步谈判，交易可能采取全面收购、追加股权投资、提供更多芯片及算力支持，或通过聘用员工并获得技术授权等多种形式。英伟达此前已向 Reflection AI 投资 8 亿美元，是其最大股东之一。 知情人士透露，双方可能在未来数周内达成协议。Reflection AI 今年 3 月融资时的估值达到 250 亿美元，其开发的开放权重 AI 模型被美国政府视为抗衡 DeepSeek 等低成本竞争对手的重要技术资源。（来源：新浪科技） 消息称 OLED 屏新款 iPad mini 售价将大幅上涨，或接近 799 美元 10 月 11 日，彭博社记者马克 · 古尔曼表示，苹果计划本月晚些时候推出新款 iPad mini。新机的起步存储空间可能会有所提升，但有意换机的用户得提前做好涨价的准备。 古尔曼透露，新款 iPad mini 售价相比现款机型将大幅上涨，预计将接近 799 美元（IT 之家注：现汇率约合 5,359 元人民币）。作为对比，现款 iPad mini 7 价格为 599 美元（现汇率约合 4,017 元人民币）/4,799 元人民币。 据悉，新款 iPad mini 将首次采用 OLED 屏幕，配备重新设计的机身。预计将拥有全新扬声器系统，搭载性能更强的芯片。（来源：IT 之家） 京东预约超 200 万人：苹果 iPhone Duo 折叠屏手机 15999 元起倒数 5 天预售 10 月 11 日，iPhone Duo 定价 15999 元起，国行 10 月 16 日晚 8 点接受预购。 京东目前预约人数已超 200 万人，需要注意的是： iPhone Duo 仅支持 eSIM 京东渠道首批可能需要签收激活（以下单时宝贝标题 / 咨询客服为准，就算不用任何补贴，也需激活后才能签收）（来源：IT 之家） 尊界：踏板升级方案预计于 10 月底确认，11 月起陆续启动升级 10 月 11 日下午，尊界客服向记者确认，尊界 V800 制动踏板支架底座升级方案预计于 10 月底确认，11 月起陆续启动升级。 10 月 8 日晚，尊界汽车发布关于尊界汽车制动踏板支架底座相关问题的情况说明，称将进一步优化该部件设计，并为已交付用户提供免费升级选择。 11 日下午，尊界客服告诉记者，目前，已提车的用户可通过全国任一服务中心预约登记，也可直接联系购车门店登记，届时用户中心将会第一时间联系用户；而未发运车辆会被直接升级后再交付，用户无需额外操作。（来源： 北京日报 ） 比亚迪李柯：五年内赶超丰田、大众 登顶全球车企销量第一 10 月 11 日，日前，比亚迪执行副总裁、国际业务负责人李柯在新加坡一场峰会上明确了公司下一阶段的全球战略目标，计划未来五年内赶超丰田和大众，成为全球最大汽车制造商。她表示，比亚迪将坚持出海战略，持续开拓欧洲、中美洲、南美洲、亚洲和大洋洲市场，并强调公司在储能、光伏、电池等多个领域实现领跑，电池技术是核心竞争力之一，优势不只在汽车。 谈到美国市场，李柯明确表示暂时不进入，原因是美国拟以立法形式强化对中国相关联网汽车及车辆软件进入美国市场的限制，即便在美国设厂的极星，也不得不转向其他市场销售。（来源：cnBeta） SpaceXAI 官方账号更名为 SpaceX Super Intelligence 10 月 11 日，马斯克当地时间

title: 12 分钟订单破万，吉利银河战舰 700，要订下新能源越野的新标准
summary: 图片来源：吉利银河 「这台车我们造了 5 年，这也是吉利第一次造越野车。」吉利汽车研究院院长李传海说到。 就在几分钟前，10 月 10 日，吉利银河战舰 700，一台新能源野车正式发布，16.98 万（限时焕新价）起的价格，让这台最高配备三电机四驱，千匹马力，能爬 45° 坡、能应急浮水的越野车，变得十分打动人心。 吉利银河战舰 700 的价格梯度比较大｜图片来源：极客公园 事实也是如此，在发布会后 12 分钟，吉利银河战舰 700 的订单数量就突破 1 万台。 但在显性成功的背后，你确实会猜测，可能恰恰因为吉利「缺乏越野基因」，才能让团队没有任何包袱，从底层架构层面，重新思考新能源时代的越野车，到底应该是什么样。或者， 用吉利团队的话，是新能源越野时代 2.0 的产品，该是怎样的 ？ 大梁，「吃」进车里 过去十几年，硬派越野车的规矩很简单。想要真越野，就上非承载式大梁，车身坐在一副独立的钢制梯形车架上，扛得住扭，经得起摔，代价是车重、空间被吃掉、进城开起来晃晃悠悠。想要舒适，就选承载式车身，好开好坐，但遇到交叉轴和连续冲击，车身容易扭，严重时车门都关不严。 新能源来了之后，这道题反而更难。电池要找地方放，电机要找地方装，大梁车本来就紧张的底盘空间被进一步压缩，车重再往上叠几百公斤。市面上不少新能源硬派，其实是在两条老路里选一条走，要么在大梁车上做加法，要么给城市 SUV 套一个方盒子外壳。 银河战舰 700 的思路，是不再二选一。 吉利集团 CEO 淦家阅介绍 GTA 架构和一体大梁技术｜图片来源：极客公园 它基于吉利新发布的 GTA 原生新能源越野架构， 核心是一套被称为「一体式大梁」的结构 。简单理解，就是把大梁拆成三段分别用最合适的工艺来做，再整体嵌进车身骨架。前纵梁用超高强热成形钢，中段是超高强辊压集成大梁，后纵梁用 TRB 热成形（一种变厚度轧制工艺，受力大的地方厚，受力小的地方薄），三段前后贯通，再和门槛梁、横梁连成一个整体。 这么做的收益体现在几组数字上。官方数据显示，这套结构的强度比传统大梁提升 30% 以上，整车扭转刚度做到 44180 N·m/deg，比同级独立大梁车型高出 20% 以上。与此同时，它比独立大梁方案轻 80 到 100 公斤，高度方向省出 40 到 70 毫米，换来更大的头部空间和 80.3% 的得房率。 它想要大梁车的「骨头」，又不想背大梁车的「包袱」。 需要说清楚的是，从结构分类上看，这依然是一台承载式车身的车，吉利早期资料里也用过「内嵌式梯形半承载」的说法。它并不是传统意义上的非承载大梁车，这套结构在长期高强度越野中的可靠性，最终还要交给时间和用户来检验。 吉利银河战舰 700 的底盘｜图片来源：极客公园 架构只是起点。新能源越野之所以值得从头设计，还因为电机能做到传统机械四驱做不到的事。 银河战舰 700 的雷神 EM-T 采用三电机布局，前面是发动机加三挡 DHT 电驱，后桥是两台独立的轮边电机，单台峰值功率 220kW。两台后电机各自控制左右车轮的扭矩，再加上前后轴之间的扭矩分配，就构成了两把随时待命的「智能软锁」；后桥另有一把电控机械差速锁，0.2 秒内完成 100% 锁止。这就是吉利所说的「两软一硬」。 专门为吉利银河战舰打造的 EM-T 混动技术｜图片来源：极客公园 传统越野车的机械锁，往往要等车轮打滑之后才介入，或者需要驾驶者提前判断、手动开启。 三电机的逻辑是在打滑发生之前，就把扭矩送到有附着力的车轮上 。顶配 2.0T 车型系统综合功率 830kW，合 1129 匹马力，在巴丹吉林沙漠的尼三锅沙山上，满载五人、零速起步、不助跑，一把直拔登顶。 底盘同样是一套为城野两头准备的组合。前双叉臂加前悬 6 点硬连接，2.0T 车型后悬也换成双叉臂，悬架行程 280mm；双腔闭式空簧负责高度和刚度，有 120mm 的升降行程，城市里降低，越野时抬高；CCD 连续可变阻尼减振器每秒调节 500 次。官方给出的麋鹿测试成绩是公路 80km/h，沙地 72.1km/h。 安全是这套架构的另一半。在一体式大梁之外，银河战舰 700 用 11 根 2200MPa 的热气胀管做了一个隐藏式防滚架，覆盖 A、B、C、D 柱、上边梁和后顶横梁，总长 10.6 米，整车顶压 161kN。李传海在群访中换算过，这大约是 16 吨，相当于整车重量的 5 倍多。电池包则做了内凹设计，底部离地 313mm，比整车最低点高出 80 毫米。 他还讲了一个细节。工程师曾在沙漠坡道上刻意把车掀翻，别的车可能要滚好几圈，而这台车翻过来一圈就停住了。原因是开发时反复推敲车宽、轮胎宽度和质心高度， 目标是先让车尽量不翻，翻了也要保住乘员舱。 这些设计背后是同一个判断，新能源越野车不是给燃油越野车「插上电」，而是要从结构开始重做一遍。 越野很酷，但大部分时间在城里 一个不太浪漫的事实是，买硬派 SUV 的人，绝大多数时间都在城里开。 吉利银河销售公司常务副总经理关久旸在群访中提到，有一类用户更在意好看的外观和时尚的内饰，驾驶场景 98% 都在城区。研发负责人的表述更直接，这台车首先要解决用户 80% 到 90% 的日常通勤，「就像一个真正的大五座 SUV」。 所以， 银河战舰 700 的智能化，首先是为城市准备的 。 高配车型搭载千里浩瀚 H7 方案，使用 Thor-U 芯片，算力 700TOPS，配备激光雷达和 29 个感知硬件，支持 D2D 车位到车位的领航辅助。从驶出车位、出入地库、通过闸机，到高速和城区 NOA，再到泊入目标车位，全程不需要人为衔接。泊车覆盖 300 多种车位类型，包括断头路车位、机械车位和极窄车位，还支持离车泊入和手机遥控的「指尖泊车」。 对一台 5 米多长、近 2 米宽的方盒子来说，这些功能的价值远比在一台普通轿车上大。 吉利银河战舰 700 的内饰设计也有很多巧思｜图片来源：极客公园 静谧性也是重点照顾的部分。路噪主动降噪、发动机主动降噪、前后排双层夹胶玻璃叠加之后，官方数据是 120km/h 时车内噪声 68.4 分贝。 把这些能力串起来的，是 EEA 4.0 电子电气架构，以及吉利基于 WAM 世界行为模型提出的「舱驾融合」思路。超级 Eva 被定义为整车的 AI 大脑，打通座舱、底盘、四驱和智驾。上车时，AI 空调会根据乘客的穿着自动调节温度和座椅加热通风；自适应底盘会识别驾驶员身份和习惯，匹配阻尼、悬架高度和转向手感。 到了野外，这套智能换了一个任务，降低门槛。研发负责人在群访里说得很实在，传统越野车对驾驶技术要求很高，攀岩时油门踩猛了不行，不敢踩也不行。 吉利银河战舰 700 甚至搭载了推进器能让车辆在浮水模式下脱困｜图片来源：极客公园 AI 全地形模式会结合摄像头和车辆动力学数据自动识别雪地、泥地、沙地、岩石路面，切换扭矩分配和油门响应；智能攀爬模式开启后，自动进入低速四驱、锁上后差速锁、把悬架升到最高，驾驶者只需要控制方向。在上饶试验场那段 100% 坡度的坡上，开启 AI 模式之后「可以不用人去驾驶」。 他们想解决的，就是一个问题——让新手司机也能开。 当然，智能化同样有配置梯度。两驱探索版不带领航辅助，探索+和 1.5T 四驱版本搭载 H5，只有 2.0T 顶峰版和陆地方舟版才配 H7。这是吉利熟悉的打法，按需求给用户分层，而不是让所有人为用不上的功能买单。 越野能力决定这台车的上限，城市体验决定它能卖给多少人。 从新能源越野

title: 马斯克豪言 SpaceX 估值将超1000万亿美元，遭拉表打脸；传腾讯字节加速个人智能体研发；四部门拟禁止汽车采用全隐藏式门把手
summary: 马斯克豪言 SpaceX 估值超 1000 万亿美元，惨遭拉表打脸 近日，马斯克在社交平台大胆预测，SpaceX 未来估值有望突破 1000 万亿美元，体量将远超当前全球经济总量。目前 SpaceX 估值仅约 2.2 万亿美元，而 2025 年全球 GDP 总量约 118 万亿美元，此番极具颠覆性的超高估值言论引发全网热议与质疑。 面对这一惊人预测，有网友晒出富国银行证券整理的一张名为「说到做到记录，以及其所隐含的折价」数据表格，直接打脸马斯克的激进预测。 表格梳理了特斯拉、SpaceX 多项核心项目，Robotaxi、Semi 卡车、星舰等重点产品的实际落地成果与马斯克此前公布的目标差距悬殊，多项项目达成率极低、交付严重延期，部分目标甚至已被撤回。 据不完全统计，马斯克在过去 15 年间提出的 602 个明确目标中，仅有约三成能够按期实现。从 Robotaxi 的多次跳票，到 Cybertruck 交付的反复推迟，再到 Semi 卡车的量产困境，「马斯克时间」早已成为科技界对过度承诺的一种调侃。 在 SpaceX 冲击更高估值之前，如何将那些「说到做到」的承诺转化为实际交付，或许是马斯克需要面对的更现实的问题。（来源: TechWeb） 消息称 Meta 已搁置向 Anthropic 出租 AI 算力的计划 10 月 10 日消息，《华尔街日报》在一篇报道中提到，Meta 已搁置向 Anthropic 出租 AI 算力的计划。 报道指出，Anthropic 首席执行官 Dario Amodei 今年早些时候曾亲自致电 Meta 首席人工智能官汪滔 (Alexandr Wang)，希望从这家竞争对手处租赁 AI 计算芯片。Meta 就此事进行过内部讨论，最终做出了暂不提供的决定。 随着 Muse 系列自研模型的逐步发布，Meta 的 AI 业务从早些时候的低潮中快速恢复，自身对算力的需求也迅速增长。此时若选择向 Anthropic 出售算力可算是「资敌」行为。 报道提到，算力资源分配正影响人工智能人才的就业选择，Transformer 架构核心作者 Noam Shazeer 之所以二次离职谷歌就与算力不足有关。与此同时，大量的算力建设承诺最终落空，限制了 AI 产业的发展。（来源：IT 之家） 消息称英伟达洽谈收购 / 追加投资 Reflection AI，加码开源模型 10 月 11 日消息，据金融时报消息，知情人士透露，英伟达正就收购美国初创公司 Reflection AI 或向其追加投资展开深入谈判。 Reflection AI 专注于开发开放权重模型，于当地时间 10 月 5 日发布旗下首款开放权重 AI 模型 Beam。 知情人士补充称，目前的谈判尚处初期阶段，潜在交易可能采取多种形式——包括所谓「人才兼并」模式。在这一架构下，英伟达将吸纳其核心团队并获取技术授权，从而绕开全面并购通常伴随的漫长反垄断审查。 英伟达目前已是 Reflection 的主要股东之一，也可能选择通过新一轮股权投资，或以提供更多芯片与算力资源的合作方案，进一步加深与该公司的绑定。英伟达此前已向 Reflection 注资 8 亿美元（现汇率约合 53.65 亿元人民币）。 据多位知情人士透露，双方有望在未来几周内敲定方案，但各方也强调谈判仍存在破裂的可能。目前具体的交易条款尚未明确，但在今年 3 月的上一轮融资中，Reflection 的估值已达 250 亿美元（现汇率约合 1,676.62 亿元人民币）。（来源：IT 之家） Muse 推出后，腾讯字节被曝加速 Personal Agent 研发 据财新最新报道，在 Meta 推出个人智能体 Muse 后，字节跳动和腾讯都在加快个人 AI Agent 产品布局。 财新从字节内部人士处了解到，字节跳动已在国庆假期前加紧推动个人智能体产品研发。相关项目代号为「Spell」，今年 4 月启动，延续了豆包手机助手此前探索的 Personal Agent 方向。目前，该项目由豆包手机助手团队主导，Spell 项目与豆包对话团队共同负责，计划将相关能力与豆包产品结合，争取尽快对外推出。 腾讯方面则已于 9 月底上线个人智能体产品 LightVela，将其定位为「云端个人助理」。该产品可以通过微信接入，全天在线处理用户的日常需求，目前仍处于开发者体验阶段，新用户可免费试用一个月。（来源：财新） 调查显示近半数美国员工夸大 AI 使用情况，只为给上司留下「懂 AI」的印象 随着企业持续加大对生成式人工智能的投入，并不断向员工强调 AI 带来的效率提升，越来越多的职场人士开始面临使用 AI 工具的压力。然而，一项最新调查显示，许多员工实际上并不清楚如何有效使用这些工具，却仍会刻意夸大甚至伪装自己的 AI 使用水平，以迎合管理层的期待。 商业智能公司 Visier 参与开展的一项研究对 1000 名美国全职员工进行了调查。结果显示，接近一半的受访者会错误报告自己在工作中使用生成式 AI 的频率和能力。Visier 将这种现象称为「表演式 AI（Performative AI）」。 数据显示，48% 的受访员工承认曾向同事或领导夸大自己使用 AI 工具的经验或熟练程度。受访者表示，这种行为背后的主要原因并非真正掌握相关技术，而是希望在 AI 时代展现自身竞争力。与此同时，他们普遍认为企业并没有提供足够的培训和明确指导，导致许多人即使被要求使用 AI，也缺乏实际操作信心。约 45% 的受访者表示，他们感受到使用 AI 的压力，但并不确信自己能够高效运用这些工具。 仅有 28% 的受访者认为雇主充分了解 AI 在工作场景中的使用方式；只有 29% 的人认为管理层真正理解员工对于 AI 的担忧；而认为上司了解员工所需培训程度的比例也只有 33%。此外，32% 的员工表示，公司尚未制定明确计划来评估 AI 对组织产生的实际影响，另有 27% 的人甚至怀疑管理层根本没有相关规划。（来源：cnBeta） 腾讯元器将于 11 月 9 日停止服务，所创建智能体将不再可用 10

title: 好产品就是与时代和生活共振｜2026 年度极客最爱好物启动
summary: 一件好产品，往往是在用过一段时间之后，才让人意识到它的好。出门时顺手带上，遇到事情时首先打开，或者因为有了它，愿意尝试一件过去觉得麻烦的事。这样的产品，值得被分享给更多人。 2026 年，我们把寻找好产品的目光，投向更丰富的形态。能协助完成任务的 AI 应用、戴在身上的智能设备，以及尝试在真实环境中干活的机器人，都进入了今年的选品视野。技术提供了新的可能，具体的产品体验，决定了人们愿不愿意把它们带进生活。 我们关注产品解决了什么问题，也在意使用它要付出多少学习和操作成本。一款创作工具，可以让想法更容易实现；一件有趣的小设备，也可以只负责让人开心。我们同样欢迎那些在设计、手感或某个小细节上做得出色的产品。 2026 年度极客最爱好物 Geek's Top Picks 正式启动。我们希望找到那些有独到想法、经得起使用，也让人愿意推荐给朋友的产品。 我们希望通过今年的推荐，发现更多让技术变得可用、让生活多一点乐趣的产品，也认识它们背后的创造者。 心智增强 一段对话、眼前的场景，或一个随时冒出的想法，都可能成为设备理解我们的线索。「心智增强」关注那些帮助人记录、理解和调用信息的产品：记住容易遗漏的细节，连接零散的知识，在需要时提供恰当的提示。我们期待它们自然地融入日常，让人少一点来回查找，多一点从容。 创作现场 拍下一段运动中的画面，换个角度观察熟悉的风景，或把屏幕上的设计做成桌上的实物，创作的乐趣常常从一次动手开始。相机、无人机、创作外设和桌面制造工具，都在这份寻找之列。我们关注它们怎样缩短想法与作品之间的距离，也在意它们能否给熟练的创作者留下更多发挥空间。 游戏人间 有些产品的价值，就是让人愿意多玩一会儿。它可能让一场游戏更尽兴，让你和宠物多一点互动，也可能让第一次观星变得容易上手。「游戏人间」想寻找这样的设备与玩具：上手有乐趣，反复玩仍有新发现，还能让人愿意叫上朋友一起试试。 开挂日常 一个人的想法，可以借助一款应用走得更远。写出第一个程序，完成一段影像，把零散资料整理成能用的知识，或把繁琐的步骤交给 AI 执行。「开挂日常」寻找让人做事更顺手的软件，也欢迎那些功能专注的小工具，让原本费力的事情变得容易。 赛博养生 睡眠、运动和恢复，是「赛博养生」今年继续关注的日常。手表、戒指、睡眠设备和运动装备，可以帮助我们更具体地了解身体状态。我们想寻找的产品，能把记录变成容易理解的信息，提供有依据、可执行的建议；也能在佩戴、充电和操作这些细节上少添麻烦，让照顾自己更容易坚持。 未来搭子 一起做事，也一起生活。我们对未来产品的期待，包含能帮上忙的助手，也包含可以交流、带来陪伴的伙伴。「未来搭子」寻找那些让人产生新鲜互动体验的产品。它可以帮助料理日常、回应好奇，也可以用一种意想不到的方式融入生活。我们期待看到，创造者如何把理解人的想法，做成具体可感的体验。 2026 年度「极客最爱好物」现已开启征集。我们将从这六个方向出发，寻找值得体验、讨论和推荐的产品，把具体的使用感受与产品故事带给大家。 候选可以是一件做工扎实的硬件、一个让人离不开的软件，也可以是一台带来新体验的机器人。产品的独到之处，需要在实际使用中得到说明。我们也欢迎小团队的作品，以及尚未被广泛认识的好产品。 如果你是产品的创造者，欢迎介绍它为谁解决了什么问题，以及目前可以体验的版本；如果你是使用者，我们更想听听，你在什么场景下用它，为什么愿意推荐它。 也欢迎推荐六类之外、有独特价值的产品。 请将产品介绍、体验方式和推荐理由发送至 geekgadget@geekpark.net 点击回顾往年极客公园 「2025 年度极客最爱好物」

title: 记录生生不息的创新力量｜2026 年度「InnoForce 50」启动
summary: 过去几年，科技行业最重要的变化之一，是创新的底层逻辑正在被重新改写。 到了 2026 年，AI 已经不只是技术变量，而成为影响产品形态和组织方式的关键变量。它开始进入办公室、工厂、汽车、机器人、医院等场景，也进入了许多过去并不处在科技叙事中心的行业。它改变软件，也反过来改变硬件；改变一个人的工作方式，也改变一家公司的组织方式。 但 AI 不是全部。真正值得被记录的，是当 AI 成为新变量之后，整个创新世界被重新点燃了。 有人从 AI 出发，做出了过去不存在的产品；有人把 AI 带进传统行业，去解决那些卡了十年、二十年的老问题；有人重新思考人与机器的关系，让机器不只是工具，而是执行者，甚至某种意义上的「新同事」；也有人并没有把 AI 放在舞台中央，却借助新的技术能力，让原本不可能的事情第一次变得可行。 这也是创新最有意思的地方：它从来不只有一种样子。 它可以是一项底层技术的突破，也可以是一款真正打动用户的产品；可以发生在企业内部的一次自我革新，也可以藏在产业链深处的关键环节；可以来自年轻创业团队的突破，也可以来自成熟公司的自我迭代。 在 2026 年这个技术快速变化的节点上，「InnoForce 50」想寻找的，是那些正在推动创新发生的人、产品、技术、组织与企业。 他们未必已经是最大的公司，也未必拥有最响亮的名字；他们可能还在一个细分领域深耕，可能刚刚完成从技术到产品的关键跨越，也可能正在产业链深处悄悄改变一个关键环节。 越是喧嚣的时代，真正的创新越值得被认真辨认。因为真正改变世界的力量，往往不是某个奇迹时刻，而是一群人长时间的投入、试错、迭代和坚持之后形成的结果。 InnoForce 50，记录生生不息的创新力量。 2026 年度「InnoForce 50」的筛选标准综合考虑了以下三个关键维度： 创新突破 寻找那些不止于微调改良，而是在技术路径、产品形态、用户体验、组织方式或产业逻辑上带来明显变化的创新。 1. 范式变化： 不是对既有产品、技术或组织模式的局部优化，而是在关键路径上形成新的解法。 2. 创造新可能： 能够打开过去难以实现、难以商业化的新场景、新市场，为用户、行业或社会创造新的增长空间。 真实价值 寻找那些已经进入真实世界、真正解决问题的创新，并创造了可验证的用户价值，而不只是停留在技术演示、概念验证中。 1. 真实需求验证： 面向明确且重要的问题，而非为了展示技术能力而制造场景。它需要证明自己解决的是用户、企业、产业或社会中真实存在的痛点，并且这一需求具有足够的广度、深度或紧迫性。 2. 可验证的落地价值： 已经在实际使用、商业部署或产业应用中体现出明确价值，包括提升效率、降低成本、改善体验、提高安全性或创造新的增长机会。 长期潜力 寻找那些不止影响当下、更能打开未来的创新。 1. 持续演进能力： 具备清晰的技术路线、产品迭代空间或生态扩展能力。它能够随着数据、算力、供应链、用户反馈的成熟而不断增强，形成可持续演进的长期系统。 2. 新品类与新赛道潜力： 有机会孕育新的产品类别、服务形态或产业分工。它可能还处于早期阶段，但已经展现出成为未来主流技术方向、产品形态、产业入口或基础设施的可能性。 根据以上标准，我们构建了 2026 年度「InnoForce 50」的「新变量坐标系」。它不是简单按行业划分，而是从产品、技术、组织、场景和全球化等角度，重新观察创新正在发生的位置。它由 10 个维度构成，是我们观察和衡量这个时代创新力量的新标尺。（ 本次筛选主要覆盖 2026 年 1 月 1 日至 2026 年 10 月 31 日期间发布、落地或取得关键进展的产品、技术、组织与解决方案。 ） 1. 年度创新产品 年度创新产品寻找那些真正创造了新价值、解决了真实问题，并对用户行为、产品形态产生重要影响的产品。 筛选标准： 真实问题与新价值： 面向明确且重要的用户需求或行业痛点，提供有效解决方案，并创造出区别于既有产品的新价值。 产品创新与体验突破： 在产品形态、交互方式、技术应用、服务流程或商业模式上具有明显创新，使用户体验、使用效率或可获得性发生实质改善。 2. 年度前沿技术突破 年度前沿技术突破寻找那些在基础科学、底层技术或关键工程能力上实现重要突破，并为未来产业变革打开新可能的技术成果。 筛选标准： 原创性 ：在科学原理、技术路径、工程实现或系统架构上具有原创贡献，而非对既有方案的简单改良。 技术壁垒 ：具备较高的研发难度、工程复杂度或知识密度，形成难以被快速复制的技术门槛。 突破意义 ：解决了长期存在的关键技术难题，或显著推进了某一领域的技术边界。 3. 年度 AI 原生硬件 年度 AI 原生硬件寻找那些因为 AI 的出现，而重新设计硬件形态、交互方式和使用体验的产品。它关注的不是简单加入 AI 功能的传统硬件，而是那些因 AI 能力而重新被定义的硬件品类。 筛选标准： AI 原生性 ：AI 是产品成立的核心前提，而非附加功能；如果没有 AI，产品的核心价值、使用场景或存在意义将明显削弱。 硬件形态重构 ：AI 能力真正改变了产品的硬件设计、交互入口或设备形态，而不是在传统硬件上增加一个智能功能。 体验质变 ：AI 带来了更自然、更主动、更个性化或更高效的使用体验，使用户与硬件之间的关系发生实质变化。 4. 年度智能体创新 年度智能体创新寻找那些让软件从「响应指令」走向「理解目标、调用工具并完成任务」的创新产品与系统。 筛选标准： 目标理解与任务规划 ：能够准确理解用户意图与任务目标，在复杂、多步骤或开放场景中进行任务拆解、路径规划，并保持目标一致性。 工具调用与执行能力 ：能够有效调用外部工具、系统、数据源或 API，完成检索、分析、操作、生成等复合任务，并具备流程推进、状态管理和结果交付能力。 真实场景价值与人机协作 ：已在真实场景中验证价值，并能形成清晰、可控、可信的人机协作机制。 5. 年度智能生产力 年度智能生产力寻找那些通过 AI、数据系统或智能工具，显著改变个人、团队或组织生产效率的产品、平台与解决方案。 筛选标准： 生产力跃迁 ：在效率、成本或质量上带来显著且可验证的提升，真正改变任务完成的速度、资源投入和结果水平。 工作方式重塑 ：扩大个人或团队的能力边界，推动新的岗位分工、协作流程、人机协同模式或组织运行方式形成。 6. 年度开发者赋能 年度开发者赋能寻找正在重新定义软件创造方式的工具、平台、开源项目与基础设施。 筛选标准： 开发效率与范式跃迁 ：显著提升代码生成、调试、测试、部署、维护或协作效率，并通过 AI Coding、智能体、自动化工作流或新型开发平台，改变开发者与代码、工具链和软件生命周期之间的关系。 生态基础设施与创造力放大 ：通过开源项目、开发者社区、云服务、框架、数据库、中间件等，为软件创新提供可复用能力，并让独立开发者、一人公司或小团队具备更强的能力。 7. 年度物理 AI 创新 年度物理 AI 创新寻找那些推动 AI 从数字世界走向物理世界，并在感知、决策、控制或执行层面取得重要进展的产品、系统与解决方案。 筛选标准： 核心能力突破 These let you import modules like so: lazy import json lazy from pathlib import Path The module will then be imported the first time those symbols are used in the code that follows. My LLM CLI tool implements plugins. I had to recommend manual lazy imports in the plugin author documentation, because simply installing plugins that used heavy dependencies such as sentence_transformers could add multiple seconds to every invocation of the llm command. Lazy imports directly address this startup cost. Unpacking in comprehensions The new [*sublist for sublist in lists] unpacking syntax is neat. summary: Danish-Lithuanian Unmanned aerial vehicle manufacturer MNP Technologijos, operating under the Monopulse brand, has raised over €2 million from investors in Lithuania and abroad. Investors included Coinvest Capital, Plug and Play, and NGL Ventures, whose angel syndicate contributed €560,000 from 68 investors, its largest syndicate to date. Founded in 2021, Monopulse develops advanced reconnaissance drones for NATO militaries, and its technology covers both aerial and water-based surveillance. Its technology focuses on making drones more reliable in electronic warfare environments, where communications and navigation signals can be disrupted or jammed. Monopulse combines aerospace engineering, electronics, sensor fusion, computer vision, and AI to develop drones capable of maintaining communications or operating autonomously when signals are lost. Its products include the Falcon MK3S drone platform, with variants for intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, and other specialist applications, alongside the Hydrohex system. summary: Scarlet , the certification body for AI and software medical devices, today announced a $50 million Series B led by Headline , with participation from new investor Notion Capital and existing investors Atomico, Creandum, Kindred Capital, and Entrepreneurs First. Nancy Xiao Mclaughlin, Partner at Headline, joins Scarlet’s board. AI medical devices are being developed faster than certification bodies can review them. A company can train an AI diagnostic model in weeks and then wait 12 to 18 months for an assessment by experts, with another six to eight months of unnecessary delay for approval of a minor update, slowing down healthcare innovation. Scarlet is a government-designated certification body. Among the roughly 52 such organisations designated under the EU Medical Device Regulation, it is, according to the company, the only one that specialises in software and AI, and was truly built to enable AI’s iterative development. Scarlet holds designations from the EU, the UK’s MHRA, and the US FDA, where it is recognised as a Third Party Review Organisation. summary: The UK AI minister today called on frontier AI labs to ramp up the safety of their leading AI systems, as the UK announced it was strengthening its cyber defences, including potential new legislation, as it prepares for potential serious AI incidents. Speaking in London today, Kanishka Narayan, the UK’s AI minister, said: “To the companies developing the world’s most powerful AI systems, my message is: Listen when your scientists warn of serious dangers. Investigate unexpected behaviour. And if you cannot adequately control the risks, do not release the system.” His warning follows OpenAI agents earlier this year going rogue, launching “unauthorised” actions against organisations, including the Australian government and Anthropic holding back the full release of a new AI model, saying it was too dangerous for the public. Narayan today said Britain must act now to strengthen its defences and prepare for future serious incidents as AI frontier models become increasingly powerful and capable of acting autonomously. summary: German energytech unicorn 1KOMMA5° has reached a valuation of $1.35 billion in its latest financing round as it prepares to increase investment in its AI-powered energy management business. This is Peter Mikhael, Founding Director of Green Mind Agency , a digital marketing agency in Cairo, Egypt. We are delivering our services to B2B, we found a gap in the Egyptian market and we fill this gap with our experience and straightforward KPIs, we are delivering services like Google Ads, Facebook Ads, Instagram Marketing, SEO, Social Media Management. What s your backstory and how did you come up with the idea? I started using the computer at the age of 12 in 1995 when Windows 3.5 dominated devices. My use of the computer developed and I learned Excel and Word and managed to do small things using Excel. After that, up to Windows XP, I was able to install the Adobe version, which contained Photoshop and Dreamweaver, which enabled me to create the first website in 2000. I was 18 years old at this time and it was a very important step for me. With the encouragement of my parents in this field, I won the third-place award for a religious website and stayed ahead of strong competitors for my age at the time. During my university studies, I self-taught some programming languages ​​such as PHP, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, which greatly improved my level in developing WordPress sites easily in 2007. After I got the job, I was very involved in meetings and discussions with clients, which helped me to understand the requirements of the clients and how to implement them. It was a golden opportunity for me to get the experience of communicating with clients and drawing up the required agreements and making modifications. At the beginning of 2008, I was able to get a job at Tarek Nour Advertising, which enabled me to expand from a website designer only to enter and gain experience in the world of digital marketing. I got to know many aspects of work, and this success earned me the silver award in 2008 for creating the best website in the field of Advertising in Egypt. In 2010, I joined Link Dot Net and also expanded my range by designing some games, creating motion graphics videos, and designing ads used in Google Display. This year I managed to get three awards for three different sites. In 2011 I was able to get the ideal job in the global company Yahoo, and for the first time after entering Egypt; I was able to learn how to manage the team, learn how to think about developing the field, organize the workflow, accelerate the process, and find suitable opportunities for customers. I learned a lot from that position. I also learned from my co-workers and managers, especially one of my managers, Mareike Schumacher . From her, I learned how to develop my performance and strategic thinking. 2014 was the year of transformation in my working life, as all the employees were laid off by Yahoo, and I took advantage of this opportunity to establish a company called Green Mind Agency. After the establishment of the company, I got acquainted with a new level of how to run an entire company and how to get clients. I also learned how to find job seekers to work in the company, and how to create a system that generates leads every month. Not only that, but how to deal with Taxes, governmental papers, and license checkups. It was an important part of my development. The goal is always unified, which is to find the best chances of success in the Digital marketing field and deliver it to our clients. After the Corona pandemic, some companies turned to digital, creating great opportunities for us to develop new services and ideas. Take us through the process of designing, prototyping, and manufacturing your first product. The field of digital marketing is a service and not a product, and this should be conveyed to your customers in the first place. In the first stage of building the company, we wanted to find the fastest way to get the tasks done. For example, the creation of websites, a special WordPress system was built and developed to be a stable template that can generate more websites in the future for potential clients. The same idea has been applied in other services we provide, we think like a customer who will buy from our company, and we need to provide the level of services expected from us. Describe the process of launching the business. The Green Mind Agency website was the first step to launching the agency. I personally gave it a priority as I knew it would reflect positively in the long run. While the focus was on designing the website, we also gave attention to establishing social channels across different platforms. We found our first client by recommendation, it was Union National Bank in Egypt, we started this project in March 2014, the same month we opened the agency. Our agency selected other agencies to build a website for the bank, we pitched the latest technologies related to website design and development and won the deal. We signed contracts also with user clients, most of them recommended our company to handle their digital marketing projects. As an individual, you need to continue improving yourself beyond university and beyond work. Quality over quantity was always the go-to since the inception of Green Mind Agency. Admittedly, the B2B clients weren’t many, but they always valued our input and our service. They usually had an enjoyable experience working with us, considering the time and effort dedicated to their project and our constant communication with them. Since launch, what has worked to attract and retain customers? If we are speaking mainly about B2B business, then Google Ads helped tremendously in reeling in more clients. However, during 2014 and 2015, Facebook and Instagram were all the rage. Although we were always trying to target B2B, these booming platforms at the time were almost exclusively B2C. Our presence on these platforms was a no-brainer, but getting B2B clients out of them was almost impossible considering the nature of their audiences. We put up content regularly and boosted the content with paid ads geared towards B2B content to try and work around this issue. We understand it was a long-term plan to generate B2B customers, and we can’t rely on only one social media channel or paid ads, we got to use all of them, in the beginning, to be able to mentor where we can spend effort. How are you doing today and what does the future look like? As of today, the world is starting to realize all the activities we do can be digitized. Not just the functions and services Green Mind Agency has to offer, but even the regular day-to-day activities. You can now order food from the comfort of your home, clothes from online stores, toys from Noon, and so on. At the same time, businesses are recognizing the need for a strong digital presence for B2B communication. This created two opportunities: The first is opening the doors to digital marketing agencies around the world to thrive, regardless of position, with only quality of service in mind. This made the digital marketing agency market much more competitive as you can work with anyone from around the world as long as they ensure the quality of the service you desire. The second point would be the shift towards the quality of services before quantity. Your delivery of one service, but excelling at it over the rest of the market is more important than offering 50 mediocre services. Through starting the business, have you learned anything particularly helpful or advantageous? The good decisions we make in the company are the ones that keep Green Mind Agency in business. The thorough selection of both employees and clients ensures a clear workflow, a strong foundation, and an encouraging atmosphere to work in. We don’t necessarily have to accept any client interested in working with Green Mind Agency. There are industries we don’t engage in and have the freedom to turn them down. Simon Sinek Want more updates on Skylead? Check out these stories: Who are you and what business did you start? My name is Kristian Zivkovic, and I am the Co-Founder of Skylead , a Sales Engagement Software that facilitates and enhances Lead Generation thanks to its multichannel outreach. Skylead allows sales professionals and anyone in search of business opportunities to generate and reach out to their leads faster and easier than ever before. By profession, I am a software engineer. However, I have always been rather drawn by innovation and change. Ever since high school, I have worked on different projects, many of which failed, but taught me valuable lessons that later lead to successfully co-founding Skylead. To witness our growth is the increase by 127% with active users from the beginning of 2021 and the fact that our team is 5 times bigger than a year and a half ago. What is your background story and how did you come up with the idea? I left school, two Universities to be precise, and a well-paid job to co-found Skylead. Skylead officially exists for 2 years and 3 months. In the beginning, it was 4 of us. We met at Belgrade’s Startup Center, where we worked on different projects. Once we came up with the idea of creating Skylead, we left our jobs. It simply seemed a better business opportunity. The idea of Lead Generation Software came up after we did some market research and realized that this branch had a lot of potential for improvement. Our goal was to think of a better solution for automated outreach. However, we did not know if our idea was the right one, how we were going to solve certain problems, or offer better solutions for some features. To validate the product we first spoke and reached out via our tool to people who wanted to test it. At that moment, the other two co-founders were in Amsterdam where they found many test users. This is when it became clear that our target audience was B2B marketers and that they will make the most out of our tool. Two of the previous co-founders were sales and marketing-oriented, while my current business partner Jovan and I were in charge of developing the product. Later on, we realized that we did not have the same vision of where we see Skylead in the future so we professionally parted ways. Initially, it was a bumpy ride. We used to stay up till sunrise for several months before the first version of Skylead was launched. As I mentioned earlier, we had well-paid jobs and we entered this project with all of our savings. Despite that, right before the first launch, we were completely moneyless. We were either going to launch it or fail miserably. Having a first-paying customer really felt good! Take us through the process of designing, prototyping, and manufacturing your first products First, we researched the existing tools that were what seemed to be our future competition. Initially, we were figuring out what features they had and tried to find better solutions. What we produced first was definitely not what we had imagined. The initial version of Skylead was way too complicated to use. That is when Jovan and I focused more on making it user-friendly. What we came up with was very basic in comparison to what Skylead has now. But the clock was ticking, we were running out of funds, and we did not have any more time to further develop the software. At least for the first release. The beginnings of Skylead Describe the process of launching the business Our initial goal was to make the software work and to find the first test users. The other two, now former co-founders, were in charge of finding people who were willing to test it free of charge. This way we could get feedback and see what was working and what needed improvement. The current co-founder and I were in charge of the development solutions. Our growth has been increasing ever since the launch, despite the software not being perfect. We were solving problems on the go. When I look back and think about the initial phase, of course, we could have done something better. It could always be better. What I’ve learned from this experience and wish I could say to my “younger self” would be to focus more on what customers say, learn from their feedback, and develop the software further from there instead of relying majorly on our vision. This would cost us working on a certain feature for months and then getting feedback that that feature was completely useless for our clients. Since launch, what has worked to attract and retain customers? Initially, we were relying only on using our tool to reach out to our potential customers. We had no public presence, which now I see as a mistake. We were still growing pretty rapidly. However, maybe if we had invested more into sales and marketing from the very start, our ROI would have been much higher. Currently, we use Facebook ads, Google ads, newsletters, Facebook, Instagram, and YouTube as far as our online presence is concerned. Also, white labeling our product still makes a major part of our revenue. The number of whitelabel users is higher than all of Skylead’s individual users together. White labeling Skylead was not available from the very start, but it is something we started around 6 months after the first sale. Our main “trick” for retaining customers has always been impeccable customer care. This is something our users have always been satisfied with. Yes, we had moments when we were understaffed and maybe customer care suffered a bit, but we were always striving to solve that problem as quickly as possible. Skylead’s Customer Care and Success Managers How are you doing today and what does the future look like? I can say that we are doing pretty well. We are profitable, have more customers, and have bigger growth. However, we are still working hard on all aspects of our business. Our customer acquisition cost is not the same for individual users and bigger clients such as businesses and done-for-you agencies. We measure “conversion” from the moment a potential user clicks on an ad until they book a demo call. The Average Conversion Rate is around $50, but it varies for individual users and bigger clients. Individual smaller users stay with us for around 4 months. Bigger users stay for a longer period of time. The majority of them are still with us since they first signed up, many of which were even over a year ago. Website monthly traffic: 22000 visitors. Average Time On Site: 1:04 Gross Margin: 90%, Skylead cost is $100 per account Ad Budget: $4,000 Customer Lifetime Value: $1576.90 The newsletter is aimed towards our existing clients, who are regularly being updated on our new features, educational and informative material (blogs and YouTube videos), and other important information. Our short-term goal is to improve our Customer Support and Success. This way we want to solve user problems quicker, hear them out, and strengthen our business relationships. Of course, we are also constantly working on fixing bugs and other minor problems in our software. Our long-term goal is to be the first fully developed and “complete” Sales Development Representative so that the individual can focus on closing the deal

If you're interested in reading how they got started, published over 6 years ago, check it out here. Hello again! Remind us who you are and what business you started. Metricool is a social media management tool that helps social media managers, freelancers, and agencies to analyze, manage and schedule their online visibility with a few clicks. Easy and intuitive. Google My Business, Instagram, Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn groups, LinkedIn personal or brand accounts, Twitch, Youtube, TikTok ads, Google ads, Facebook ads, etc. Hi! I m Juan Pablo Tejela, CEO at Metricool . Metricool is an online tool that helps manage social media and advertising platforms through analytics and from a single site. It’s directed towards a wide range of users from small businesses to social media managers. From a business point of view, Metricool is a SaaS with a Freemium model. You can either register for free or subscribe to one of our Premium plans with more features and brands available. My wife and I embarked on the Metricool adventure 5 years ago and now we have over 800,000 users, more than 15,000 subscribers and we have exceeded $2.8 million in ARR (Annual Recurring Revenue). Tell us about what you’ve been up to! Has the business been growing? In the last year and a half, our ARR has increased from $1 million to $2.8 million. The number of users has doubled and we have almost tripled our revenue and customers. So, we are thrilled to see the pace at which we are growing and evolving in this short period of time. This growth is partially the result of having reinforced our internationalization strategies, especially in LATAM and the US, while we have maintained our SEO and social media marketing strategies and kept looking for strategic collaborations. However, our product is the main reason for this progress which keeps our customers loyal to our tool and encourages them to stay with us longer. We launch new features and updates every month, some of them have come as a solution to the issues or suggestions that our users raise through our live support chat. Listening to them is a fantastic resource for improvement and inspiration. Apart from adding new functionalities to our tool, we have also integrated new trendy platforms such as Twitch and TikTok Ads. Also, as a Google Partner, we have added Smart Bidding to our Google Ads campaigns. However, our two great achievements this year are the inclusion of the auto-publication on Instagram and the launch of our new mobile app. It has been an exciting year so far, a wonderful non-stop that has been possible thanks to a great team of professionals, a family that keeps growing. This year, we have added six new talented members to our developing, marketing, and customer support teams. Improving our product and including new features, while keeping excellent customer service support is key to making all this happen and win our customers hearts. Cumulative monthly active users since Jan 1, 2020 What have been your biggest lessons learned in the last year? Without a doubt, the biggest lesson has been Flexibility. COVID19 has taught us to adapt quickly to changes and be flexible with our customers, colleagues, and the needs of the market. One of the biggest consequences is that currently, the whole metricool team is working remotely, which has also allowed us to find talent thousands of kilometers apart. This change has been key and the results have been excellent. We have also ratified two of the company s key values: Our product and the team. Having a good product is vital because customers pick up on it fast and it is where we can contribute the greatest value. On the other side, having a great, motivated, trained, and the autonomous team is key to making this happen. Investing time in training and listening to the team’s ideas brings sensational results. As a personal challenge, I cycle for 40 mins and walk an average of 20,000 steps every day: a sound mind in a sound body. What’s in the plans for the upcoming year, and the next 5 years? Our next challenge is to reach and increase our presence in other European countries and reinforce the strategy in other regions such as the United States and LATAM. We will undoubtedly continue to invest in the product, in our road map we have already marked the following milestones: social inbox management and more options for online advertising campaigns. Set your goals in the medium-long term. For us, the projection in five years has to follow the original line, keep growing sustainably. Have you read any good books in the last year? I mostly listen to podcasts and my top 3 are: Saaster - Interviews where they share stories of companies similar to ours, inspiring case studies from which you can learn a lot. Itnig - Equivalent to Saaster but with case studies of European and Spanish companies. Product Hackers - Focused on growth techniques for companies, where there are also interesting interviews and success stories. Advice for other entrepreneurs who might be struggling to grow their business? Set your goals in the medium-long term. We are often too anxious to see immediate results and we put our efforts into short-term strategies that are not sustainable over time. I have seen other companies in our niche that are based on functionalities that violate the policies and terms of use established by social platforms. They grow fast, but their decline is just as fast. What works for Metricool is to design solid and long-term strategies, making sure that every step we take keeps us on the right path. Maybe we will go slower but I am certain that we will get further. Are you looking to hire for certain positions right now? The idea is to incorporate native people from the countries in which we plan our internationalization. Both to enrich the company and also help us better understand the country where we want to focus. Where can we go to learn more? [Update] How This Fulfilment Company Survived To Fires, Floods And Forced Relocations (2022) ➜ Hello! Who are you and what business did you start? Helloooooooooooooo!!! I’m Philip Karageorgis and I’m the founder of Honest FulPhilment - a sourcing, branding, and fulfillment company based in China, managed in the UK! If I had to choose, I’d say our flagship service is the combination of sourcing, branding, and fulfillment for our clients. We effortlessly transform their slow, dull and undistinguishable customer experience into a quick, exciting and instantly recognizable branded one. We manage and handle every aspect so that it’s not daunting to our clients making the switch. Communication is clear, concise and they know exactly what’s involved, together with the cost. To top it off is located in China means we offer exceptional value even though our customer service standards are very high. Our customers are drop shippers, eCommerce store owners, and even other miscellaneous sourcing companies who white label our services We started with a team of only 4 in 2019, learning on the job, investing our own time and money to grow the business. Considering we didn’t run any marketing campaigns or concentrate on lead generation by other means, surprisingly, we saw consistent growth and demand for our services. We’re lucky to see our revenue increase each quarter and look forward to when we can start actually running marketing campaigns on multiple platforms! What s your backstory and how did you come up with the idea? I’ve never been one who enjoys working set hours and being employed by others. I always saw it as a means to an end. In saying this, I certainly benefited from some of my 9-5s, the skills I acquired and learned the importance of processes, systems, and policies. Taking the career path, climbing up ladders, kissing butt was never my forte. I can’t think of anything more depressing than working for the same organization for what feels like an eternity, with minuscule promotions or pay raises. Don’t get me wrong, some enjoy this path, after all, it’s stable, consistent, and brings security - as with everything, there are pros and cons. From the age of 16 I tried many things, from selling car parts to reselling hydroponic equipment, I ultimately lost money in all ventures (all of which I was doing while working full time). Most of this came down to inexperience and just not doing things properly. Fast forward many years and jobs later, my friend introduced me to affiliate marketing. After 6 months of studying and trying, I failed. The same friend then gave me a dropshipping course he paid for but didn’t yet have time to look into. Considering I failed with affiliate marketing (while he was still killing it), and giving up on rate race freedom wasn’t an option, I dove in head first! Long story short, I saw very early success. This was the game-changer for me. Something was actually working, FINALLY! My mindset completely changed. I couldn t actually believe I was generating sales, let alone making money. Pumping more advertising spend resulted in even more revenue, things quickly changed and I soon handed in my notice at the day job to concentrate on e-commerce full time. Shortly after resigning, I moved to China (I lived there for over the year 2007-2009, so it was an easy move knowing the language and culture) to be closer to the ground. In doing this, I was able to test products and turn around campaigns much quicker. Wasn’t plain sailing though, shit hit the fan and my success died out. Fun times were a lot of crazy and interesting characters started to mingle. To be interested in Bitcoin that early, you generally had to be a bit “out there”. Germany however, pretty quickly proved itself to be true to its well-earned reputation to be a pretty horrible starting place for innovative entrepreneurship; a regulatory quagmire that leaves little room for the necessary quick, fast, and cost-efficient iterations you need to execute as a startup. So the first wave of Bitcoin entrepreneurs left Germany for greener pastures in Amsterdam, Switzerland, London, or, in our case, Vietnam. Building a Bitcoin exchange service was a pretty obvious idea at the time since access to Bitcoin was still extremely limited - it was a time where Mt. Gox in Japan was still responsible for 90% of the world s trading volume! Basic infrastructure was lacking - and we were determined to build a part of it. This gave us some pretty decent initial insights on the state of the market (extremely immature with no professional services around). Hi guys, we are Marc and Bennett Schneider, father and son co-founders of Dioxyme (btw it is pronounced Dye-Oh-Zyme) and we manufacture and distribute DTC and B2B, small-batch, craft, nutritional supplements. The Dioxyme story began with a son’s dream to play pro hockey, and his father’s unrelenting desire to help make that dream a reality. Bennett began each day knowing he had to work harder than the next guy. He understood he was not gifted with innate special talents other than hard work and a dream. He worked day in and day out on his speed, size, strength, and skills. All the while, Marc watched, motivated, and helped. He learned about the game, sports training, nutrition, and how to make his son the best athlete possible. Bennett left home to further his dream, working his way up the ranks from prep school to junior hockey. He was always looking for a leg up on the competition. To help, Marc usually had something up his sleeve. New training techniques, better nutrition, different workouts. Everything would lead to improvements… except for supplements. Somehow, supplements never made any difference in his son’s training or game. Marc, a surgeon, patent holder, and somewhat of a mad scientist, could not understand why, so he dug into it. Scientific studies proved many ingredients could help his son. Unfortunately, most supplement companies didn’t use those ingredients in their products, and if they did, it was at the wrong dose. “Snake oil.” So, the mad scientist bought raw ingredients and began mixing and trying his own formulations. And... MPO - Muscle Performance Optimizer was born. They were stunned. The homemade concoction made a real difference in the gym and on the ice. Hi, my name is Alexi, in 2004 I launched AwardWallet with my then business partner Todd Mera. AwardWallet is an online service that automates the process of tracking loyalty points such as frequent flier miles, credit card points, hotel points, etc. The solution itself is free to use but there are additional features that are enabled for users who buy AwardWallet Plus, a yearly subscription for $30 / year. In addition to this in-app purchase, we monetize our users via affiliate marketing by offering them credit cards that offer the best sign-up bonuses and earning capabilities. In addition to providing a B2C solution, we package our parsing technology into APIs that we sell to other businesses. Has the business been growing? Since we last spoke, AwardWallet lost about 21% of revenue due to Covid in 2020. It is tough to be in the travel space during a pandemic when no one is allowed to travel. Today is June 22, 2021, and business has picked up significantly, as a matter of fact, June is shaping up to be our biggest month ever. However, we won’t see a full recovery until business and international travel returns to pre-Covid levels which are still going to take quite some time. It didn’t make sense to invest anything into growing our user base during the pandemic, as travel was the last thing people were thinking about. Instead, we focused on developing the product, we tackled some big items that we were putting off before the pandemic. Develop an idea in your head, start building, and don’t stop. Just find inspiration or motivation to do it and do it. To better understand when travel is going to come back we created and published a set of reports that reflect how much our users are traveling, as that closely correlates with how much they use AwardWallet. These reports can still be found here . This report shows how many active air bookings our users track on AwardWallet on average per 1000 users. As of today, July 22, 2021, we can already see that July is the biggest month in terms of travel since the start of the pandemic, though still not at the pre-Covid level. Here are a few things that we released during covid: We added discounted flight deals in our mobile apps (iOS and Android). Tap Menu - “Discounted Flight Deals” to see it. Added the ability to import all loyalty point expiration dates into the calendar of your choice like Google Calendar. Added the ability to track parking reservations via AwardWallet. Added dark mode to our Android app, which we were lacking for quite some time. Added the ability to gift AwardWallet Plus to a friend . Added the ability to scan our users’ mailboxes (after they grant us that permission) for new loyalty accounts, so right after the registration, our users don’t need to guess which programs they are a member of. We can now tell them that including their account numbers (in many cases) so that all they have to do is provide us with passwords to those programs so we can start tracking them. Added an option to reveal passwords in our mobile interface, integrated with native keychain technology for maximum security. Added an option to export an excel file that lists all the countries (with dates) that a user visited in the last 10 years. This report can be found under our Trips section in the left menu in our web interface . What have been your biggest lessons learned in the last year? Even though it may generate 30% of our revenue in some years we can’t rely on this revenue going forward. All it took was a decision by a couple of banks to not pay affiliate revenue (or drop their commission rates) and our affiliate revenue just disappeared almost instantly. Next big hit was on the B2B (APIs) side of the business. Some partners that used to pay for our API all of a sudden we re not able to pay anymore. It became very apparent which ones were affected the most by Covid. Some went bankrupt, some had to cancel or put contracts on hold, and some, on the other hand, were just fine. What surprised me the most was that while our AwardWallet Plus revenue (in app purchase) did not grow in 2020 it also did not drop during Covid. So I started valuing that revenue stream much more after Covid as it proved to be the most resilient. We obviously lost some customers due to Covid but we also got some new ones and in the end, we broke even. The other thing that Covid taught me is the value of diversification. I decided that going forward we are going to diversify our business even more, as much as potentially getting into other businesses that can use similar technology to what we already built. I am actively pursuing two new opportunities not related to AwardWallet directly just because they would diversify our portfolio and would hopefully make it much easier to survive the next force majeure event. On a personal level, there is nothing that I achieved during Covid that I am proud of, I gained about 15 pounds and started drinking more. The only good thing is that due to the lack of travel I worked more and I spent more time with my kids. I became a kindergarten teacher for my daughter, as well as a cook and a nurse. Our current backlog of features, as always, is very long so we need to decide what to prioritize next. With a background in medicine, as well as finance, over the past years, we as a family invested in companies relatively successfully. This gave us a solid foundation to be able to invest in a new venture ourselves. Understanding the unmet needs of patients but also healthy people, we invested the first money to start Bloom. Later, some great, renowned investors joined our journey. This is not about a quick shot, but about a long-term development, which is here to fundamentally change healthcare. Recently, we launched the first tests in the first pharmacies in Austria and are seeing overwhelmingly positive feedback from our users. Also, we are launching the first Bloom Store in Zurich to allow customers to learn more about the products. Take us through the process of designing this device. In healthcare, especially if the hardware is involved, it takes a while to develop products. Regulatory requirements are very strict and you need Quality Management (QM) from the beginning. We were able to build an exceptional QM, due to having an exceptional team. You cannot start any design of a product without having implemented it in the QM System, which by the way is audited. So it was a great step to receive the ISO Certifications proving the quality of our development and certifying us a medical Company. Later in 2020, we received the CE mark for our first products. The idea and design evolved. The path to success is characterized by fast learning and improving what you are developing without much compromise, aiming to achieve the highest standards. But eHealth is here to stay, and as with smartphones, there will be a strong integration of different services alongside testing, as ePrescriptions, telemedicine, and much more. Also, with the growing field of personalized medicine, diagnostics in the future will be linked much closer to personalized therapies. And this is exactly what Bloom is preparing for. Partners as pharmacies are curious and glad to receive support with some evidence, as a test result, when they advise about e.g. supplements. After over three years of development, it is very gratifying to see the first excited customers. It took time and capital, but, as said, we are speaking about an overall disruption where people can better understand their health issues. They will always be guided to doctors in case of need. Only quality and a great experience will retain the customer. The customer is our focus. But as mentioned previously, the great challenge is creating awareness. Search for the best possible people, including human factors, surround yourself with them and never be afraid to hire people who are better than you. They have to be. The long-term goal is to become the premier free flipping resource for resellers. I started building KickFlips in January of 2021 and launched in late February. After that summer, I started looking for ways to make money that didn’t involve manual labor in a field during the summer heat. I discovered flipping items off Craigslist . Looking back, it was wild that my parents were ok with my 16-year-old brother driving me to meet strangers in parking lots to buy and sell things. But, after the first few profitable flips, I was hooked. I could make more in 30 minutes than I made in a full day on the farm. I started looking into other ways to make money flipping items and eventually stumbled onto sneakers. Over the years, I’ve had countless friends ask me to show them how to make money flipping sneakers, video game consoles, GPUs, and more. I knew from a past business that if everybody inquires as to how you do something, then there is a market for your knowledge. I got so many people asking me to teach them, that it became crystal clear there was a large, untapped market for people who are interested in learning to flip sneakers. Sneaker-reselling communities and resources already existed, but were all too expensive or ineffective. A $5 texting service didn’t offer any help to someone new to sneaker-flipping. A $99/month Discord group membership was far too rich for anybody who simply wanted to test the waters for the first time. There didn’t seem to be a decent free resource, so that was the logical market position to target. Take us through the process of designing, prototyping, and manufacturing your first product. The first step was to figure out the most effective medium to deliver this information. Texting is not a rich enough form of communication. Facebook groups and Slack channels require too much hands-on management. Email is the best medium for what I was trying to convey. Eventually, I added a Discord channel for Pro members, which I believe was a huge value-add. In true entrepreneurial fashion, I figured that if I was going to practice web design, I may as well get paid for it. Thus, I reached out to a handful of local companies to redesign their website. The biggest prototype challenge was figuring out which features to include in the free version and which features to include in the Pro version. If you give too much value to the free group, then there’s insufficient incentive for your customers to upgrade. If you give too little, then they will assume that the paid version also can’t be that great and they’ll unsubscribe altogether. This is still a dance I’m figuring out, but it’s important to strike a good balance in that regard. Describe the process of launching the business. There was no pre-launch email capture, no Facebook / Instagram ads, no big campaign, or anything remotely resembling an actual business. It was definitely an amateur show. Despite my lackluster “launch”, the word-of-mouth snowball started growing slowly. After a month, I had already amassed a couple of hundred subscribers - 100% organically. More importantly, I had a very strong paid upgrade rate of well over 10%. In my eyes, this upgrade rate seemed to validate the business model I had chosen. After all, 1,000 true fans is better than 10,000 passive customers . My “big break” came 2-3 months after launching KickFlips . My name is Shiloh Johnson I am the founder, and CEO of ComplYant and we help business owners navigate the messy world of tax compliance using technology. We supply our customers with customized tax calendars that guide them through what forms are due, when, and how much they can expect to pay for those tax bills. We also help them save for the coming bills and process payment when ready to be filed. Currently, our revenue is at $28k monthly recurring revenue in just eight months from launch. What s your backstory and how did you come up with the idea? I have sort of a non-conventional background in accounting. I have an undergrad degree in accounting and a graduate degree in taxation. The average accounting student would go work for a big four accounting firm after graduation, working 18 hours a day during tax season and then continue to work their way up the ladder. However, because I was a young mom and had to work my way (full-time) through college, I couldn’t work 18 hour days during any season with a family. So I pivoted, taking a tax clerking job with an in-house tax team and working my way up that way. I spent 13 years working for large corporations like Aramark and Technicolor. I worked in their in-house tax teams, handling everything from sales and income tax to annual reports and business licenses. And for large corporations that have multiple locations and nexus in just about every state, it was no easy feat. I then went on to start my own tax practice serving small business clients that had crazy tax issues. For example, I had a client that thought that she could collect sales tax from her customers and not pay it to the state. She reasoned that she read somewhere that food wasn’t taxable. What she missed was that prepared food is taxable. She also missed how absolutely illegal it is to collect tax from a customer and not remit it to the state. So that was a $50k mistake, and there were so many more like it. I remember thinking, how can I help more business owners navigate the early years of a business . The rules in tax are the same for both small and large businesses, the difference is large companies have the infrastructure to hire a team of knowledgeable support to keep them out of hot water. So I decided to build that for small entrepreneurs. I started jotting down ideas, sketching designs on a yellow notepad. I spent $10k for a dev team to make the first version. I got the money from my tax business, it was going well and I learned how to live on little and use the rest for the app. So I was working on client work during the day and ComplYant at night. Oh, I just realized the irony. I tried to avoid 18 hour work days for the sake of my kids, only to wind up working 18-hour workdays. But thankfully, my kids were teenagers so they were fine not having me around as much. Take us through the process of designing, prototyping, and manufacturing your first product. I’d love to tell you that the first version of the app flourished and I made lots of money. But I didn’t, it tanked. I had 50 people download it and test it and it was horrible. They didn’t understand it and didn’t like it and I had a certified failure on my hands. Not to mention a wasted $10k (yea that one hurt). So I scrapped it and went back to the drawing board. Here’s a tip: don’t pay to be a part of anyone’s accelerator or incubator that is not offering you investment. I then asked 100 people to trade time and advice in exchange for allowing me to pick their brains about how they manage their tax as entrepreneurs. I was trying to get to the root of what a paying user really needed. And it was unanimous: they needed to know what tax responsibilities they were required to pay, when to pay them, and how to save the most money in the process. So that is what I built. We tested the product on those interviewees and that’s when I knew I had something good. I also learned that what I think people need doesn’t matter. What they are telling you they want matters so much more. I found the first development team that helped me suss out my ideas into wireframes on Upwork. They were a Russian-based team and they did fine, I really didn’t care how it looked, I just wanted it to work. And it did work, it just wasn’t any good. Around the same time, a new accelerator program promising to help people build version ones of their product offered me a spot in the program to which I had to pay $800 to be a part. Here’s a tip: don’t pay to be a part of anyone’s accelerator or incubator that isn’t offering investment. Also, you get what you pay for. I’m not sure why I thought $800 was going to get me a better version of the product. I finished the program with absolutely nothing. But I still wasn’t defeated. I went back to the drawing board. I was back on Upwork and this time I looked for one developer with Laravel experience. That was what version one was built on and the only coding language I knew. I also narrowed down my search to coders in the US because US tax rules are more complex than anywhere else in the world, and I needed to make sure my dev understood that. I took all of my interview responses to my new coder and he helped me get through the basic version 1.5, a customized tax calendar. We also moved the product from a mobile app to a desktop platform. Then I tested it on people and charged for it. I figured if they’d pay then they really needed it and it would be worth continuing to build. I was right. At that point, the product was earning $2300 monthly recurring revenue and I was so amped. To me, that was enough money to prove that I could build something great and that I was ready to raise outside investment. Describe the process of launching the business. We build a feature, we test it, and then we release it to the public and get feedback about it from customers. The time frame from when I first had the initial idea to when I incorporated was one week. I move fast. I’ve learned not to be afraid to put something in front of customers, that is really the only way to figure out if it’s any good. From that time to the horrible version was three months. I told myself that I wouldn’t quit supporting my clients until I could secure enough funding that allowed me to pay myself. And after a year I was able to do just that. I’ve learned not to be afraid to put something in front of customers, that is really the only way to figure out if it’s any good. Obsessing over something that no one has seen is a waste of time. I m Joel Fickson Ngozo, a software engineer, innovator, and techpreneur. I m the founder and the developer of Vwaza Multimedia , a startup company offering media streaming services for African creators targeting a global audience. Vwaza empowers African Creators by helping them have a platform through which they can distribute music and poems. Launched on June 9th, 2021, Vwaza has 220 plus listeners from Africa, the USA, Europe, and China, and over 100 artists from over 5 African countries. Vwaza has two sections: Vwaza Creator, and Vwaza Listener. Vwaza Creator is an artist section where African Artists can upload their content. Content can be music albums, eps, and singles, and even poem collections. This content is streamed through the Vwaza Listeners App available on both Web and Mobile (Android and iOS). Listeners will start buying the music through our web platform and artists will be getting revenue from sales that are empowered by us. What s your backstory and how did you come up with the idea? In 2020 I posted on Twitter and Facebook of an idea that would empower African creators in the music business by making sure they would earn something. I looked at how most digital distribution platforms don t really pay artists that well and let alone African Artists. This is how the idea came up. I received a lot of motivation from so many people telling me that I should develop the app. So I embarked on the journey of developing it. I once was a rapper and I have friends who always complain about their music not selling or even getting nothing out of it. That combined with my technical expertise in programming, I began developing the web app and later on started working on the mobile app. Since I m close to so many friends who are into music, I sent them the beta for them to try it out and give feedback. It was great because they really loved it and that kind of helped me a lot in the whole development life cycle. Throughout the whole development process, I have been bootstrapping the business by paying for Google Workspace , Google Cloud Storage and even servers just to keep the platform alive. Take us through the process of designing, prototyping, and manufacturing Vwaza Multimedia. After the mock-up designs were shared on social media, I took some time to start thinking of the tech stack that will be used to develop this platform. I wanted to have a web platform first for artists and then create the app to be used by Listeners. The tech stack was identified as React, MongoDB for the database, and Nodejs as a backend framework. The music uploaded is to be stored on Google Cloud Storage. So I started coding the web app( www.vwaza.com ). I didn t have web designs for this, it was straight from my mind and being coded. The initial MVP to be developed was going to have a few features which included streaming singles, albums, and checking out artists who had registered. So, it was developed. On the other side, I made sure that the artist s platform was done as well and they were able to upload music with ease. I would say, GET STARTED. I love saying that imperfect is perfect and you really have to move fast and break things as Mark Zuckerberg says. Shared below are some of the first screenshots of both the web and mobile app. Describe the process of launching the business. Vwaza was launched on June 9th. The goal was an organic launch. As a bootstrapped business, Vwaza hasn t received any sort of funding but solely relied on personal funds raised through freelancing that I do. The biggest lesson learned throughout the whole process is that there were a lot of people who encouraged me to develop the platform but few really managed to be a part of it. User conversion and retention has been a very big issue Since launch, what has worked to attract and retain customers? We have often seen a surge in growth or traffic every time we publish a new update or we post on our social media that we are working on something new. Even though we haven t done a lot of marketing, our organic reach has been very effective in a way. Our Google Analytics has shown us that we do better at every update we do. How are you doing today and what does the future look like? We are doing pretty well aside from onboarding creators/artists. The main challenge we do have now is integrating payment methods. Africa is diverse and it has a lot of country-specific regulations and we are trying so hard to make sure we deal with that in a way that speaks to every artist. One of our main goals is to make sure we empower our African creators through revenue generated on the platform. To do that we need to move from being a free platform and ensure that our artists can sell their content. We hope by the end of the year 2021, we will have payments done and see our artists get their share of the money. In the next few months, we will be working with individual artists and try to diversify our operations from audio and navigate also into a video for Africa among other things. Through starting the business, have you learned anything particularly helpful or advantageous? Personally, I have just applied what I have learned previously in other business ventures. I may have no co-founder at this point because I have learned that choosing a co-founder should be one of the most crucial decisions one must make. If you choose the wrong one then you are heading downhill and that might be the downfall of everything. I think choosing to work with independent contractors is one of the best decisions I ve made so far as it prevents me from dealing with people that aren t committed to the project. I don t want people who just want to gain something and are not willing to put in the work. I would rather pay the people and have them do the best job they can do. I’m Sarah Feoli, the founder, and owner of Rescue Chocolate . My company produces B Corp-certified dark chocolate bars which are only for humans to enjoy, but all of our profits are donated to various animal rescue organizations. I sell direct to consumers on my website and at various food festivals. I also sell to a few specialty retail shops. Since my first month of operations (January 2010), I have partnered with more than 700 nonprofits to aid in their lifesaving programs. Tell us about what you’ve been up to! Has the business been growing? The business has not grown or declined during the past few years. We have reached a natural plateau, and it is a comfortable place to be for our model. I hope that those businesses that did experience hardships can come back with a vengeance! I have introduced a couple of new flavors, including a successful “paleo” bar using almond butter. Some flavors which had been put on the backburner have snuck back into the line-up, such as the Pick Me! Pepper bar. The advertising channel that never disappoints is email marketing. I use Mailchimp. The platform is very good about keeping the best customers engaged. Or else, maybe I just have a very loyal following by this time. But each campaign leads to reliable sales, especially those containing discounts. What have been your biggest lessons learned in the last year? The last year taught us all that is truly important: health, community, and compassion. In the face of a horrific pandemic and heartbreaking social upheaval, I questioned the importance of a trivial little luxury such as a chocolate bar. After the George Floyd murder and the resurgence of the Black Lives Matter movement, I delved into the legacy of cacao and sugar farming, which is not pretty in terms of the exploitation of people of color . It is heartening to know that Rescue Chocolate ingredients are fair-trade, and that is a pretty good indication of non-exploitative practices. I was also uplifted to see so many animal shelters with empty cages during the first few months of the lockdown. Single and isolated people came to rely on the companionship of furry friends. I hope the majority of those pandemic pals became permanent family members. Thanks to the continued support of my customers, I realized that 2 ounces of vegan chocolate are not so trivial after all. It can be a sweet spot of brightness when the rest of the world is dark. Not relying on brick-and-mortar traffic, my business did not suffer during the economic downtown. I hope that those businesses that did experience hardships can come back with a vengeance! What’s in the plans for the upcoming year, and the next 5 years? I hope to continue to partner with new animal rescue organizations on their fundraising programs. I am eagerly tracking the progress of No-Kill 2025 which is an initiative to make all the animal control facilities in America achieve a save rate of at least 90% by the year 2025. Despite incredible gains in recent times, there are still millions of healthy, lovable dogs and cats put to death in this country. When the no-kill goal is achieved, there will still be a role for Rescue Chocolate to play, advocating for such issues as abolishing puppy mills and getting yard dogs off their chains. I also want to keep abreast of exciting new food trends and new ingredients for my chocolate bars, to keep my products fresh and attractive for all of us who rely on our daily chocolate fix. Have you read any good books in the last year? These books aren’t specifically business-oriented. But somehow they put me in a frame of mind that makes everything seem more possible: Breath (by James Nestor), because I love breathwork and breathing meditations. I get a clearer mind and better perspective when doing so. Untamed (by Glennon Doyle) is a great reminder to live your life as fully and beautifully as possible, told in a unique voice. The Signature of All Things (by Elizabeth Gilbert), a masterful and wide-ranging tale following one character through her whole life, with interesting tidbits of science woven in. Hunt Gather Parent (by Michaeleen Doucleff), which is about how various cultures pass wisdom down to new generations. In contrast, the current American model makes it seem like all learning is starting from scratch. Advice for other entrepreneurs who might be struggling to grow their business? This may go against everything people are taught in business school, but what has worked for me has been an aversion to risk-taking. Of course, there was a risk in starting the company: outlying money with no guarantee of a return. But since proving the concept, I have been conservative. My forays into non-chocolate products (energy bars, dog-themed artwork, tee-shirts, and tote bags with the company logo) reinforced the lesson that I should just stick with a sure thing: chocolate! This strategy probably will not turn Rescue Chocolate into a unicorn, but it will ensure that the company doesn’t fall into the bankruptcy hole where the majority of new enterprises do unfortunately tumble.
